summary: Luciano Petech was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He held posts at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946), Sapienza University of Rome (from 1955), and served as president of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (~1989–1995).

Lucy Annette Jones worked in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University, studying under doctoral supervisors Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod, committee member Helena Michie, and teacher Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche (1996–1997).

Ludo Rocher was an Indologist who earned his D.Jur. and Ph.D. at Ghent University (~1944–1950). He worked at the Free University of Brussels (~1951–1966) and the University of Pennsylvania as a professor (~1966–1996) and emeritus professor (~1996–2016).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist who studied under Walther Schubring at the University of Hamburg (~1926–1928) and Heinrich Lüders at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1930–1935). In 1950, he succeeded Schubring to take a chair at the University of Hamburg.
Ludwig Heller was an Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1887–1894). He later held a post at the University of Greifswald (~1897–1934).

Ludwig Lange was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University and the University of Göttingen (~1843–1847) under Theodor Benfey, later holding posts at Göttingen, Charles University, the University of Giessen, and Leipzig University (~1871–1885).

Ludwig Wittgenstein worked in philosophy. After studies including the University of Manchester and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1911–1913), he held posts at Trinity College, Cambridge (1929–1947) and the University of Cambridge (1939–1947).
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He held a post as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

Luigi Suali was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bologna (~1900–1904) and under Hermann Jacobi (~1904–1906). He held a post at the University of Pavia from ~1907 to 1951.

Luis Oscar Gómez worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees at the University of Puerto Rico, Yale University under Stanley Insler, and the University of Michigan. He held professorships at Michigan (~1976–2008) and directed the Mangalam Research Center (~2010–2017).

Luise Hercus was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at St Anne's College (~1944–1948) and the Australian National University, where she later served as a Reader in the Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (~1969–1991).
Lungten Dubgyur is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He completed his studies at Sherubtse College, Government Law College, Mumbai (LL.B), and the University of Edinburgh (LL.M).
Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a figure in Tibetology and religious studies. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot and throne-holder from ~1969 to 2017.

Lynn A. Struve is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Washington (~1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (~1968–1976), and held a faculty post at Indiana University from ~1977 to 2010.

Lynn Thomas is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Lancaster University and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford in 1987. She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

Léon Feer was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1865), the Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872).

Léon Vandermeersch was a Sinologist and philosopher who studied at Paris Law Faculty, INALCO, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held academic posts at the University of Provence (~1970–1973), Paris Diderot (~1973–1979), and EPHE (~1979–1993).
M. D. Balasubrahmanyam was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his dissertation in 1969 at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he also held a post attested in 1967.
M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1907–1911) and served as Professor of History at the University of Mysore (attested 1910).
M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1967–1978). She subsequently held a post at King's College London from ~1990 to 2014.
